content.short: OKcontract generates plug-and-play frontends for smart contract interactions, embeddable in apps.
content.description: OKcontract makes smart contracts accessible to every app by supplying an interaction layer that automatically generates plug-and-play frontends for smart contract actions. These frontends can be embedded in both consumer and business software, reducing integration effort for developers. It supports major EVM chains and rollups, delivering comprehensive client-side infrastructure for DeFi, NFT, gaming, and SocialFi projects. Common interactions include swaps, staking, adding liquidity, minting, and claiming rewards, enabling smooth on-chain experiences inside apps.

resources.title: The Attack Surface Has Moved to Vault Infrastructure
resources.tldr: A $6M exploit that never touched the contract logic. Vault accounting, stale asset values and strategy adapters are where the real surface now sits.

resources.title: Can ERC-4626 Exploits Be Prevented?
resources.tldr: Uses a live oracle-manipulation exploit on an Aave fork to ask whether the vault standard itself invites this class of bug, or whether the integrators do.

resources.title: Valid Signatures Are Not Enough
resources.tldr: Forty major hacks in a single month, around $647M, and a good number of them were correctly signed transactions.
